title: Screen time and problem behaviors in children: exploring the mediating role of sleep duration
authors: Guerrero MD, Barnes JD, Chaput JP, Tremblay MS
journal: International Journal of Behavioral Nutrition and Physical Activity

primary_models.name: Negative binomial SEM (direct effects) of eight CBCL syndrome raw scores on social media time, adjusted for other screen types, sleep duration, and demographics
primary_models.location_in_paper: Table 2 (pp. 5-6), Social media rows; Fig. 1 (p. 7); interpreted in Results p. 3 and Discussion pp. 3-7
primary_models.design: Cross-sectional, ABCD baseline only. IV, mediator (sleep duration), and DVs all measured at the same visit; one observation per child. The direct effect of social media on each CBCL syndrome comes from a single multivariate path model in which all six screen-time variables predict sleep duration and all eight CBCL scales, and sleep duration predicts all eight CBCL scales.
primary_models.sample: ABCD baseline (2016-2018) data; paper cites NIMH Data Archive DOI 10.15154/1412097 but does not name the release number. Full baseline sample N = 11,875 children aged 9-10 years (mean age 9.91, SD .62); missing values (<1%) were replaced by multiple imputation, so the model is fit on the full sample. Table 1: sex (n = 11,869) 5681 female, 6188 male; ethnicity (n = 11,755) 6176 White, 1779 African American, 2047 Hispanic, 255 Asian, 1498 multiracial. Mean parental income category 7.22 (SD 2.42; n = 10,857), parental education 17.06 (SD 2.67; n = 11,858), BMI 18.80 (SD 4.17; n = 11,832), physical activity 3.49 active days/week (SD 2.32; n = 11,844). Social media item n = 11,769.
primary_models.iv: Child self-reported social media time from the Youth Screen Time Survey (14 items). Social media is a composite of three items collapsed by the authors because of low use: texting, visiting social networking sites (e.g., Twitter, Instagram), and video chat (e.g., FaceTime); all three components are phone/SM items, so the composite qualifies under FT-IC2 Step 2. Each item asked hours on a typical weekday and weekend day on a 7-point scale (none, <30 min, 30 min, 1 h, 2 h, 3 h, >=4 h); daily time = (weekday hours x 5 + weekend hours x 2)/7. The Methods state ST behaviors were then categorized into four groups (<1 h, 1-1.99 h, 2-2.99 h, >=3 h) for analysis, yet the Results interpret coefficients as 'every one hour increase'; the exact coding entering the model is therefore ambiguous. Table 1 (p. 4): social media M = .54 h/day (SD 1.15); text .22 (.54), social networking sites .12 (.42), video chat .19 (.49).
primary_models.dv: Eight parent-reported CBCL syndrome scales scored as RAW counts (not T-scores), modeled as negative binomial counts. Table 1 (n = 11,864) M (SD): anxious/depressed 2.52 (3.01; range 0-26); withdrawn/depressed 1.03 (1.71; 0-15); somatic complaints 1.49 (1.95; 0-16); social problems 1.62 (2.27; 0-18); thought problems 1.62 (2.19; 0-18); attention problems 2.98 (3.49; 0-20); rule-breaking 1.19 (1.86; 0-20); aggressive 3.26 (4.35; 0-36).

covariates.detail: White, African American, Hispanic, Asian, Multiracial; coding not reported

covariates.name: Other screen-time variables (simultaneous)
covariates.detail: All six ST predictors (television/movies, videos, video games, social media, mature-rated video games, R-rated movies) enter the same SEM simultaneously, so each is adjusted for the others

covariates.name: Sleep duration (for CBCL outcomes)
covariates.detail: Parent-reported hours of sleep enters as a mediator; the social media -> CBCL coefficient in Table 2 is the direct effect net of sleep duration

primary_models.equation: log E[CBCL_k] = b0k + b1k*SocialMedia + b2k*TV/movies + b3k*Videos + b4k*VideoGames + b5k*MatureVideoGames + b6k*RratedMovies + b7k*SleepDuration + b8k*sex + b9k*ethnicity + b10k*parent_ed + b11k*income + b12k*BMI + b13k*PA, CBCL_k ~ negative binomial, k = 1..8 syndrome scales, estimated jointly with the sleep-duration equation (M2). Focal term: b1k (direct effect); IRR = exp(b1k).
primary_models.estimation: Mplus 8.2 single structural equation model with negative binomial distribution for the eight CBCL count outcomes (overdispersion), maximum likelihood with robust standard errors (MLR), TYPE = COMPLEX to account for non-independence of observations (clustering variable not named; presumably site or family). Multiple imputation for <1% missing data. Mediation via MODEL INDIRECT, with bootstrapping (B = 5000) for 95% CIs run without TYPE = COMPLEX because Mplus 8.2 does not allow both. IRRs are exponentiated B. Significance at p <= .05 with CI excluding zero (bold in tables). No multiple-comparison correction. No interaction or stratified analyses. No sensitivity analyses reported. Covariate associations are in Additional file 1 (not bundled in the PDF).

d_transformation.conversion_formula: M1: IRR treated as OR at first approximation, d = ln(IRR) * sqrt(3)/pi (Chinn 2000), with ln(IRR) = B; CI on d from the printed B CI endpoints, d_lo/hi = B_lo/hi * sqrt(3)/pi. M2: beta_std = B * SD_IV / SD_DV, d = 2*beta_std / sqrt(1 - beta_std^2). M3: not converted.
d_transformation.contrast_type: Per one unit of the social media variable, which the authors describe as one hour/day; the Methods also state ST was categorized into four groups (<1 h, 1-1.99 h, 2-2.99 h, >=3 h), so one unit may be one category step.
d_transformation.notes: SD_IV = 1.15 h/day for social media and SD_DV = 1.11 h for sleep duration and CBCL raw-score SDs are from Table 1 (p. 4), full baseline sample (n = 11,769 for social media, 11,869 for sleep, 11,864 for CBCL). CBCL scales are raw scores, not T-scores, so SD_DV is not 10. The M2 conversion assumes the IV is in hours/day; if the model used the 4-category coding, SD_IV in hours is the wrong scale. The IRR->d approximation for negative binomial count outcomes is rough and ignores overdispersion. The aggressive behavior CI (.029, .053) printed in Table 2 excludes its own point estimate (.06), so its d CI should be treated with caution. M3 indirect effects are products of paths across a linear and a log-link equation with no standardized metric reported; not convertible to d. Completion pass (2026-10-01): all printed values verified against Tables 1-3; iv_type set to continuous for M1-M3; no SEs printed anywhere in the paper; IRR-scale CIs not printed (log-scale B CIs are).

extraction_flags:
It has three cards, all from one Mplus negative binomial SEM:
- M1: 8 direct effects of social media on the 8 CBCL raw scales. The metric is IRR, and B with its CI is stored alongside.
- M2: the social media -> sleep duration path. The metric is B.
- M3: 8 indirect effects of social media through sleep, none significant.

Please check:
(1) The IV units are unclear. The Methods say screen-time behaviors were binned into 4 groups (<1, 1-1.99, 2-2.99, >=3 h), but the Results read coefficients as per one hour. The SD_IV of 1.15 h/day comes from Table 1 and may be on the wrong scale for converting M2.
(2) Table 2 prints the CIs on the B (log) scale only. No IRR CI is printed, so IRR_lo and IRR_hi are null.
(3) In Table 2, the CI for social media -> aggressive behavior is printed as (.029, .053), which excludes its own B of .06. This looks like a typo in the paper. I copied it as printed.
(4) The paper does not state the distribution of the sleep-duration path. I assumed it is linear, yet Table 2 still prints an 'IRR' of .968 for it.
(5) Social media is a composite of texting, social networking sites, and video chat. All three are phone/SM items, so it qualifies under FT-IC2 Step 2. There are no per-item estimates.
(6) The CBCL outcomes are raw counts, not T-scores. SD_DV values come from Table 1, which uses the full baseline sample. Converting IRR to d via Chinn is only a rough approximation for negative binomial outcomes.
(7) The ABCD release number is not stated, and the TYPE=COMPLEX cluster variable is not named.
(8) Supplement Additional file 1 was not bundled in the PDF.

I checked every social media number against the PDF text layer (Tables 2 and 3) and all of them match.
